title: Relative Tor amplitude is detected by simultaneous source and base prime localizations
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $K^\bullet$ be an arbitrary complex of $A$-modules, and let $a\le b$ be integers. Work in the unbounded derived categories of modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], computing derived tensors by K-flat resolutions [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. For a prime $\mathfrak q\subset A$, put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$ and let $K^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}$ be termwise localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], with scalars restricted by the induced map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak q}$. The following are equivalent: (1) $H^i(K^\bullet\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N)=0$ for every $R$-module $N$ in degree zero and every $i\notin[a,b]$; (2) for every prime $\mathfrak q\subset A$, $H^i(K^\bullet_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}^{\mathbf L}L)=0$ for every $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module $L$ in degree zero and every $i\notin[a,b]$. No flatness, finiteness or boundedness assumption on the map or complex is required.

source.place: Tag 0B67, lemma-tor-amplitude-localization, equivalence of (1) and (2), renaming the base A to R and the algebra B to A.

proof.text: For any $R$-module $N$, [lem-pc-source-module-kflat-resolution] supplies a K-flat resolution $P\to N[0]$ over $R$. By [lem-trf-relative-tensor-test-model-restriction], $C_N=\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes_R P)$ is an $A$-complex whose restriction represents $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N$, including the $A$-action. For every ring $B$, multiplicative subset $T$ and $B$-complex $E$, localization is additive by fractions and exact by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives $H^i(T^{-1}E)\cong T^{-1}H^i(E)$, without boundedness; in particular it preserves quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0B67, lemma-tor-amplitude-localization, equivalence of (1) and (2), renaming the base A to R and the algebra B to A.

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak q\subset A$, $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}\mathfrak q$. By [lem-trf-relative-tensor-localized-resolution-comparison], the localized augmentation $P_{\mathfrak p}\to N_{\mathfrak p}[0]$ is a K-flat resolution over $R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $Q((C_N)_{\mathfrak q})\cong Q(\operatorname{Tot}(K_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}P_{\mathfrak p}))$ in $D(A_{\mathfrak q})$. Apply cohomology [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and restrict scalars to $R_{\mathfrak p}$: restriction leaves kernels and images unchanged, hence also cohomology. Now use Step 1's localization formula and [lem-trf-relative-tensor-test-model-restriction] over $R_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak q}$. Thus $H^i(C_N)_{\mathfrak q}\cong H^i(K_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}^{\mathbf L}N_{\mathfrak p})$. Both sides use the stated contracted-prime structural map.

source.place: Tag 0B67, lemma-tor-amplitude-localization, equivalence of (1) and (2), renaming the base A to R and the algebra B to A.

proof.text: Assume (1). Given $\mathfrak q$ and an $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module $L$, use $N=\operatorname{Res}_R L$ in Step 2. Then $N_{\mathfrak p}\cong L$: the inverse fraction maps are $l/t\mapsto t^{-1}l$ and $l\mapsto l/1$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Each denominator already acts invertibly. For $i\notin[a,b]$, (1) makes $H^i(C_N)=0$, so Step 2 gives $H^i(K_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}^{\mathbf L}L)=0$. This proves (2).
